subject: film
intro: Film leads into the screen industries' core crew: the producers and directors who steer productions, the editors and camera operators who make the images, the writers who start them and the sound recordists who finish them.

roles.title: Producers and Directors
roles.what: Produce or direct stage, television, radio, video or film productions, responsible for the creative decisions — interpretation of script, choice of actors, set design, sound, special effects and choreography.
roles.where: The key elements of film form — cinematography, mise-en-scène, editing, sound, performance — are the vocabulary directors use to realise a vision; the auteur specialist study teaches the interpretive stance the role demands.

roles.title: Film and Video Editors
roles.what: Edit moving images on film, video or other media, organising images with a producer or director for final production and editing or synchronising soundtracks with the images.
roles.where: Editing sits at the heart of the key elements of film form; the meaning-and-response strand teaches why a cut changes what an audience feels — the judgment editors apply to every timeline.

roles.title: Camera Operators, Television, Video, and Film
roles.what: Operate television, video or film cameras to record the images and scenes that television, video and film productions are built from.
roles.where: Cinematography including lighting is taught as one of the specification's core film-form elements — framing, movement and exposure — and the production unit puts you behind the camera on a short film.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Originate and prepare written material such as scripts, stories and advertisements — for film specialists, the screenplays and treatments that productions are made from.
roles.where: The screenplay pathway in the production unit pairs the narrative specialist studies — classical, experimental, alternative forms — with the craft of building story, character and dialogue for the screen.

roles.title: Sound Engineering Technicians
roles.what: Assemble and operate equipment to record, synchronise, mix, edit or reproduce sound, including music, voices or sound effects, for theater, video, film, television, podcasts and other productions.
roles.where: Sound is one of the specification's core film-form elements; the production unit's short film and its evaluative analysis train the recording and post-production decisions the role executes.
